metadata.title: Bitcoin Slips Below $69K For First Time Since August: Is This A Buying Opportunity Or A Deeper Crypto Rout?

content.text:
Bitcoin Slips Below $69K For First Time Since August: Is This A Buying Opportunity Or A Deeper Crypto Rout?
-
Ethereum prices slipped to $1,912.54.
-
According to The Kobeissi Letter, the selling pressure led to a loss of about $150 billion in crypto markets over 48 hours.
-
Crypto-linked equities, including Strategy, Bitmine Immersion Technologies, Strive, Coinbase and Robinhood Markets, fell alongside cryptocurrencies.
Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $69,000 late Thursday for the first time since August as multiple headwinds, including inflation concerns, rising interest rates, and the ongoing challenges around Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), weighed on the asset.
BTC prices slumped nearly 7% over the past day, falling to $68,529.96 at the time of writing. Meanwhile, Ethereum (ETH) prices slipped to $1,912.54.
According to market commentator The Kobeissi Letter, the selling pressure led to a loss of about $150 billion in crypto markets over 48 hours.
Crypto Bulls Are Buying The Dip In Bitcoin
Although Bitcoin is falling to its lowest level in months, some experts believe that now is a good time to enter.
Crypto analyst Michaël van de Poppe said in a post on X that he has been buying BTC, outlining five reasons for his move.
He noted that the "terrible sentiment" around the underlying asset means it is hard for prices to keep declining, adding that while there have been multiple events for the asset price to crash, it hasn't yet and markets are simply witnessing a 20% correction.
He also pointed out that this is a support area, "just barely beneath the 200-Day MA and ideal for liquidity."
The analyst said that Bitcoin had already bottomed on the Friday prior to the SpaceX IPO and that he "wouldn't be surprised" if the present scenario was at the same cadence.
"Fifthly: Nasdaq is already up a lot, meaning that there's a gap between Bitcoin and the Nasdaq. It doesn't take long for this gap to close, which is why I've been buying Bitcoin today," he said.
Meanwhile, Anthony Pompliano, Founder and CEO of Professional Capital Management, said in a post on X, "Bitcoin is falling to prices we haven't seen since…..3 months ago. Everyone relax, so you can realize that AI and bitcoin are one big trade now."
Critics Are Sceptical About The Digital Asset's Future
However, long-time crypto critic Peter Schiff is not convinced. In a post on X, he implored investors to think about how Bitcoin has been trading relative to 2021.
"Think about this, HOLDers. Bitcoin just traded at a lower price than it traded in November 2021. How many of you who owned Bitcoin back then expected it to be below the Nov. 2021 high more than five years later? Bitcoin is in a long-term bear market. The long-term trend is down," he argued.
